(`grep -n cpms-disposable-demo .github/workflows/pilot-gate.yml` finds no install step).
The only code this PR adds is the companion, which that job cannot load.

**What actually failed, in its own words.**
`FAIL journey-A1-public — stage=hold-countdown … otp/verify http=200; v1/availability
http=200; booking/quote http=200 slot_id=5803 clinician_id=19 location_id=17;
booking/hold http=404 code=CLINIC_NOT_FOUND …`. The same workflow passed three times in
a row on this branch (`fc67496` 15:07Z, `2bf9bf2` 15:37Z, `c4d4652` 16:04Z) and failed
once (16:29Z), on a head whose only difference is documentation. The failing run is also
the run whose own logs show a different environment: `cached browser binaries did not
launch on this runner`, then 68 s installing browser dependencies. Wall-clock differs by
25 minutes; the fixture is deterministic and produced identical ids in both runs
(`DAY2_FIXTURE_OK clinic_a=16 clinic_b=17 …`).

**What the 404 can and cannot be.** `booking/hold` returns `CLINIC_NOT_FOUND` (404) from
five distinct places in `BookingService`: a missing slot row, a slot whose Clinic differs
from the clinician's home Clinic without an active participation, a Clinic whose
Organization is not `active`, a Location that is not an active Clinic-owned Location, or
a slot that is no longer `is_open` (capacity). The fixture inserts the Organization as
`active`, gives both Clinics that Organization, and seeds the slot with `clinic_id` =
clinic A and `location_id` = Location A1 — the values the failing request sent. The
harness records the error **code** but not the response **message**, and every one of
those five sites uses that same code, so the evidence in hand **cannot** distinguish
"the slot was no longer open" from "the Clinic/Organization check failed". I am not
calling this fixed, and I am not calling it flaky: it is one failure, in a job that
never executes this PR's code, with a different runner environment, and the decisive
detail is not recorded anywhere readable from here. The concrete improvement that would
settle it is a one-line change in `clinic-practice-management/bin/pilot-day2-workflows.py`
(record `message` beside `code`); it is outside this PR's scope and I have not made it.

**The boundary is now smaller as well as guarded.** Reviewing the buffer rather than
trusting it: the production portal shells (`src/Frontend/*Controller.php`) render their
own document and `exit` on `template_redirect` priority 1, and their templates are the
only ones that close `</body>` — so no WordPress hook can reach those pages and an output
buffer is the only way to render a boundary without modifying production code. What
changed in this round:
- the buffer starts on `template_redirect` **priority 0** instead of `init`: it now runs
  before the portal controllers and **never exists for REST, admin-ajax, the admin
  screens or `wp-login.php`**, which do not fire that hook — JSON can no longer be
  inspected at all, let alone altered;
- `nocache_headers()` for a persona request, because the page now carries a
  session-scoped nonce and must not be stored by a shared page cache;
- a `content-disposition:` guard, so a download body is never decorated;
- `render_boundary()` (the theme path) carries the same `\Throwable` guard the buffer
  handler already had, so the banner can never take a page down on either path;
- the harness now proves the buffer end to end: no buffer and no private marking for an
  administrator request, exactly one buffer for a persona request, `nocache_headers()`
  called once, and the flushed page carrying the banner **before `</body>`**.

### [2026-11-05] — M5 / M6 / M11 clinic-scoped patient session authority (branch `arena/a96afd0f-doctor`)

- **Scope:** patient sessions are bound to one Clinic. OTP verification stamps `cpms_clinic_id` onto the issued `WP_Session_Tokens` token (`PatientSessionScope`, cookie-issue arming in `OtpService::verify`). Without a marker, the scope falls back to the distinct Clinic count of durable `cpms_patient_user_links` (1 = that Clinic, 0 = empty read, more than 1 = `CLINIC_SCOPE_REQUIRED`, HTTP 400, clinic-name-free). Application-password sessions and non-OTP `wp_signon` sessions are never stamped.
- **M5 booking:** `/appointments/mine`, reschedule-options, reschedule, and cancel resolve the Clinic from the session. For `confirm`, `resume`, `cancel`, `patient_change_deadlines`, `reschedule_options`, and patient `rescheduleAs`, the order is: object existence (404 `CLINIC_NOT_FOUND`), active durable ownership (403 `CLINIC_PERMISSION_DENIED`), then session-to-Clinic match (400 `CLINIC_SCOPE_REQUIRED`). The scope refusal happens before status, window, or expiry checks, `releaseHold`, idempotency consumption, or any mutation. `ScopeRequiredException` is preserved through `BookingService::toBookingException()`. `PublicBookingShortcode` publishes `session_clinic_id`; the client gates holds on a session/Clinic match, renders a clinic-scoped chooser, and shows the OTP step only when the session does not match the booking Clinic.
- **M6 notifications:** pure-patient actors ignore ambient `ScopeContext`. Reads are filtered to the session Clinic and fail closed for multi-Clinic sessions without a marker. `markRead` requires a single session Clinic and filters by `clinic_id` and the actor's linked patients, so cross-Clinic IDs are a no-op. Dual-role staff+patient users keep the staff `ScopeContext` behaviour.
- **Tests added:** `tests/Unit/PatientSessionScopeUnitTest.php` (pure-PHP, using the constructor callable seams, including application-password exclusion); `tests/Integration/PatientSessionScopeIntegrationTest.php` (M11 stamping, rotation, non-OTP sessions, logout; M5 session matrix, REST `mine`, cancel and deadline ordering; M6 inbox, `markRead`, hostile ambient scope); `cpms_test_seed_patient_session()` in `tests/integration-bootstrap.php`, used by six existing integration suites for non-OTP 0-link, cross-Clinic, and two-Clinic fixtures; JS source-gate and VM-sandboxed discovery tests; `bin/pilot-slice3-chooser.py` now asserts chooser suppression for un-scoped two-Clinic password logins and stamps `cpms_clinic_id` onto `session_tokens`.
- **Local evidence:** Node specs `cpms-public-booking-discovery.spec.js`, `pkg-p3-location-first.spec.js`, and `day2-portal-workflows.spec.js` passed. `python3 -m py_compile` passed on `pilot-slice3-chooser.py`. `bin/tenant-tripwire.py` exited 0 (three pre-existing suspects in untouched files). `.github/scripts/companion-isolation.py` passed.
- **NOT RUN locally:** no PHP runtime is available in this environment. PHPUnit (Unit and Integration), PHPStan, and PHPCS/WPCS were NOT executed here. The new PHP files were checked only for balanced brackets. Final-head CI is the source of truth; no PASS is asserted for PHP until it is green.
- **Not covered by the new integration file (covered by other suites or pending):** the public shortcode `session_clinic_id` render and the hidden OTP step (`Phase8Slice2OtpHoldConfirmRedTest` T22/T23 and `pilot-otp-journey.py:369`); a full OTP request-verify round trip through `OtpService` (only the stamping hooks are exercised directly); dual-role staff+patient inbox behaviour.

  - **M12 (`WooCommerceAdminAccess`):** فیلترِ جداگانهٔ `allow_own_profile_for_cpms_staff` روی `woocommerce_prevent_admin_access` و متدِ خالصِ `decide_own_profile()` اضافه شد تا فقط وقتی `prevent === true`، کاربر وارد شده، صفحه دقیقاً `profile.php`، پارامتر `user_id` تهی یا برابرِ شناسهٔ عددیِ خودِ کاربر، و کاربر دارای دست‌کم یک capability از `RolesAndCapabilities::ALL_CAPS` است، مسدودسازیِ WooCommerce به `false` باز شود. `PAGES` (۱۵ برگه)، `allow_authorized_cpms_page`، `guardWpAdmin`، مسیرهای AJAX/admin-post/سایر برگه‌های پیشخوان، `user-edit.php`، کاربرانِ فقط-بیمار و کاربرانِ صرفاً دارای نقشِ سفارشیِ مطب بدون تغییر و بسته ماندند.
- **اعتبارسنجی:** روی commit میانی `439749f`، Unit Tests (PHP 8.1–8.5)، PHPStan، Compatibility gate، Release Artifact، Standalone package contract، Tenant Tripwire، Real WordPress integration (`mysql-8` و `mariadb-11.4.13`)، Real WP Acceptance (`wp_` و `clinic_`) و Staging Gate سبز شدند؛ دو گیتِ شکست‌خوردهٔ مرتبط با تغییرات این شاخه (`WPCS (changed code)` با ۱۳ مورد روی خطوط افزودهٔ `App.php` و `Integration (WP 7.1 + MySQL 8)` با ۳ شکست در `AppActivationDatabaseGateTest` به‌علت نامِ نادرستِ جدول `cpms_op_log` به‌جای `cpms_operational_logs`) در commit بعدی اصلاح شدند. در sandbox محلی، PHP runtime و دیتابیس وجود ندارد (فقط lint و تستِ دودِ خالص با `php-wasm-cli`، بازتولید محلی WPCS با خروجی ۰ تخلف روی خطوط افزوده، `tenant-tripwire` و `companion-isolation.py` اجرا شدند؛ PHPUnit/PHPStan محلی **NOT RUN**).
- **تحویل و موارد باز:** Draft PR #325 باز و **NOT MERGED** است. رندرِ زندهٔ صفحهٔ `wp_die` در مرورگر روی صفحهٔ افزونه‌های وردپرس و خروجیِ واقعیِ `wp plugin activate` روی موتورِ نامعتبر در این محیط قابلِ اجرای زنده نبود و برای آزمونِ دستیِ نصاب فهرست شده است.

Current schema on an unsupported engine keeps serving and shows the admin notice; unreadable/garbled version evidence does not block runtime (logs throttled `CPMS_DB_ENGINE_EVIDENCE_UNREADABLE` via `OpLogger`) while activation refusal remains fail-closed. Hardened `*_for_tests` seams (`App::can_use_test_seam_frame()` + write/read guards) so they require `PHP_SAPI === 'cli'`, active PHPUnit / `WP_TESTS_DOMAIN` runtime, and a caller frame in `ClinicCore\Tests\*` or `<plugin>/tests/`.

### [2026-11-05 UTC] — PR #325 CI integration follow-up: REST server backup/restore in `AppActivationDatabaseGateTest` and live-dependency rebind in `App` service factories

- **Verified CI root cause on `7d622af0e0ca4979c484d324461f900fd4b7cc83`:** `WPCS (changed code)`, `Static Analysis (PHPStan)`, `Unit Tests (PHP 8.1..8.5)`, `Real WordPress integration`, `Real WP Acceptance`, and `Staging Gate` passed (`31/45`), while `Integration (WP 7.1 + MySQL 8)` reported 4 failures in `ClassicV1CriticalRemediationTest` (`Tests: 2644, Failures: 4`) because `AppActivationDatabaseGateTest` (`A*`, alphabetically before `Backup*Test`) initialized `$GLOBALS['wp_rest_server']` and function-local `static` services (`App::otpService()`, `App::bookingService()`, etc.) before `Backup*Test` reset `App`'s private static singletons (`$providers`, `$smsService`, `$settingsFactory`, `$db`), leaving downstream REST/service callers bound to the pre-reset `SmsService` / `SmsProviderRegistry`.

### [2026-11-06] — Capacity and hold counters: HoldsExpireHandler released capacity without an affected-rows check (B2)

- **State first:** fresh analysis on `main` `3fce6a0f87bf7646e055f1e4f197a9b0baa4bd7f` (resolved through the API: `git/ref/heads/main`). Branch `arena/def41229-doctor` was fast-forwarded to that commit; working tree clean before edits. The local clone was shallow and had to be unshallowed to compare against `main` — `git fetch --unshallow`, no reset/clean/rebase/force.
- **B2 root cause (confirmed by measurement, not inference):** `src/Application/Jobs/HoldsExpireHandler.php:33-40` guarded the slot release with `if (!$updated)`, where `$updated` came from `CpmsDb::query()`. That method returns `bool` — `$this->wpdb->query($sql) !== false` (`src/Infrastructure/Db/CpmsDb.php:86`). WordPress's `wpdb::query()` returns the affected-row count for an `UPDATE`, so a conditional `UPDATE` that matched **zero** rows returns `0`, and `0 !== false` is `true`. The handler therefore read "matched nothing" as "I changed the row" and released one unit of capacity anyway. Class **B (pre-existing)** — the code path predates this task and no test covered it.
- **Fix (minimal, inside the existing transaction/lock style):** the status `UPDATE` now goes through `CpmsDb::execute()` (which returns the affected-row count, `CpmsDb.php:99`), and the release runs only when `$changed >= 1`. The release itself keeps `GREATEST(held_count - 1, 0)` and `AND held_count > 0`, so the counter cannot go below zero. The `transactional()` wrapper, the conditional `WHERE` clauses and the per-hold loop are unchanged; the operation stays idempotent because a hold whose row no longer matches `status = 'active'` affects zero rows and releases nothing. The handler's return value (`$freed`) now counts only holds actually expired.
- **Tests added:** `tests/Unit/HoldsExpireHandlerCapacityTest.php` — 8 tests, 21 assertions. The production SQL is executed, not mocked: a stub `wpdb` (global namespace, WordPress base class absent in the plain unit bootstrap) forwards statements to an in-memory SQLite mirror with the production column definitions, `query()` returns the changed-row count like the real class, and a `GREATEST()` shim provides MySQL's variadic maximum. Covered: positive control (1 expired hold → 1 unit, 1 freed); second run on the same hold does not decrement again; hold **converted** mid-run does not release capacity; hold already **released** does not release capacity; a zero-row status `UPDATE` is treated as no change; two expired holds release two units; an unexpired hold is untouched; the counter never goes below zero.
- **RED evidence (measured):** with `git checkout --` restoring the pre-fix handler, the same file reports `Tests: 8, Assertions: 17, Failures: 3` — `testHoldConvertedMidRunDoesNotReleaseCapacity`, `testAlreadyReleasedHoldDoesNotReleaseCapacity`, `testZeroRowUpdateIsTreatedAsNoChange`. After the fix: `Tests: 8, Assertions: 21`, `OK`. The other five pass both before and after by design (positive control, the documented no-op second run, the two-hold and unexpired cases, and the floor case); the three that fail before the fix are the ones that encode the defect.
- **Unit suite scope, stated plainly:** the full Unit suite cannot be green in this sandbox — it runs on PHP 8.5.12 from an unpacked WebAssembly CLI with no `vendor/` and no database, and reports `Tests: 1053, Errors: 74, Failures: 19`. The failure-name set is **identical** before and after my change (measured by stashing and re-running: 94 names in both runs, `diff` empty), so the +8 tests are the only delta and no new failure is attributable to this change. Integration tests were **NOT RUN** — they require the WP test library and a live MySQL server, neither available here.
- **D10 — no code change, and the premise is wrong.** `docs/state-machines/appointment.md` invariant I-1 says `آزادسازی Slot فقط با T4/T5/T6` (slot release happens ONLY on T4/T5/T6), and the T8 row's side effects are `Audit؛ (آمار)` — no slot release. The code agrees: `BookingService::markNoShowByStaff` (`BookingService.php:1936-1996`) updates the appointment status and writes the audit row, with no `releaseBooking()` call, and its docblock states `Slot counters are not mutated`. `VisitService::markAppointmentNoShow` (`VisitService.php:1973-1986`) likewise mutates no counter. Existing integration assertions already pin this: `Phase7Fr55NoShowRedTest.php:255-256` asserts `booked_count` and `held_count` are unchanged by a no-show. So "no_show releases capacity exactly once" would be a change of documented policy, not a fix — reported, not implemented, per the stop condition. Concurrent cancel-after-no-show is impossible by construction: `no_show` is a terminal state and `AppointmentMachine` forbids every transition out of it (`AppointmentMachineTest.php:70`). I did not touch `BookingService.php` (PR #326 edits it).
- **Debts found, not fixed:** (B3) `cpms_slot_holds` has no unique index on holder + slot — only `u_hold_token` on `token` (`src/Migrations/2026_09_05_0001_initial_schema.php:215`); a unique index or migration is out of scope here and is recorded as a debt only. Also unproven by this work: InnoDB row-lock and inter-worker transaction isolation around the release, which only the Integration suite against real MySQL can establish.

### [2026-11-06] — Capacity counters round 2: HoldsExpireHandler DB-error handling, no-show backend decision recorded, verification debts

- **State first:** branch `arena/def41229-doctor` at `af229a3b` (PR #328, draft) when this round started; `main` was `3fce6a0f87bf7646e055f1e4f197a9b0baa4bd7f` and had moved to `8df5c19a4ce7f21111b6be29445bce6836ef4d5e` (PR #326, "Bind patient sessions to one Clinic") before push, so the branch was merged with `origin/main` using a **merge commit** (forward-only; no reset, no rebase, no force).
- **Task 1 — telling a real DB error from zero affected rows.** Read in full: `HoldsExpireHandler`, `CpmsDb` (`query()` at :86, `execute()` at :99, `transactional()` at :225, `undo()` at :277, `ensureNoSqlError()`/`setStrict()` at :37-51), and `JobsDispatcher` + `JobQueue::fail()`. `CpmsDb::execute()` in soft mode converts every SQL error to `0`; only Strict mode throws. **It is possible to tell the two apart without changing `CpmsDb` semantics:** WordPress documents `wpdb::$last_error` as "empty string if no error" and clears it on success, and `wpdb::query()` calls `flush()` *before* executing, which resets `last_error` (`class-wpdb.php:1953`, verified against wordpress-develop). So after any write, a non-empty `last_error` belongs to that statement. `CpmsDb::wpdb()` already exposes the handle read-only, so the handler can observe it without touching `CpmsDb` and without affecting any other caller. The one boundary case is a query that `wpdb` rejects *before* `flush()` (empty query, or text that cannot be stripped) — that path (`class-wpdb.php:2275-2290`) leaves `last_error` untouched, so stale state is treated conservatively as an error; the consequence is a hold that stays active, never extra capacity freed. Nothing was changed in `CpmsDb`.
- **Change (production, minimal):** `HoldsExpireHandler::guardedWrite()` wraps the two writes: it snapshots `last_error`, calls the unchanged `CpmsDb::execute()`, and throws `RuntimeException` only when `last_error` changed to a non-empty value. Both the hold-status UPDATE and the slot-release UPDATE now go through it. The existing `$changed < 1` early return is untouched, so a *legitimate* zero-row slot release (slot already at the floor of zero) still lets the hold expire — verified explicitly. On error the throw propagates into `transactional()`, which ROLLBACKs that hold only, `$freed` is never incremented, and the loop's other holds are unaffected because the transaction is per hold. The job then goes through `JobsDispatcher` → `JobQueue::fail()` → retry with backoff, and the hold is still `active` so the retry can succeed.
- **Task 2 — failure-injection tests (RED measured).** Extended the existing SQLite-mirror stub with a `writeFault` hook that fails a matching statement the way `wpdb` does (returns `false`, sets `last_error`, leaves the row untouched). Three tests added to `tests/Unit/HoldsExpireHandlerCapacityTest.php`: `testHoldStatusUpdateErrorAbortsWithoutReleasingCapacity`, `testSlotReleaseUpdateErrorRollsBackTheHoldStatusChange`, `testRecoveryAfterDbErrorSucceedsOnTheNextRun` (positive control for the error path). **Measured RED:** with the committed pre-change handler restored by file copy, `Tests: 11, Assertions: 24, Failures: 3` — all three new tests fail with "a real DB error must abort the run, not be treated as zero affected rows". **Measured GREEN** after the change: `Tests: 11, Assertions: 34`. The old code's actual data outcome on a slot-update error was also probed directly: `freed=1 hold_status=expired held_count=1` — the hold was marked expired, counted as freed, yet the slot kept counting it, so capacity was silently lost and never retried. That is the defect the tests now pin.
- **Suite honesty:** full Unit suite in this sandbox (PHP 8.5.12 WASM, no `vendor/`, no DB) reports `Tests: 1056, Assertions: 271745, Errors: 74, Failures: 19` against a baseline of `Tests: 1045, ...` at the same head; the failure-name sets are **identical** (95 names in both runs, `diff` empty), so the new tests are the only delta. Integration tests are **NOT RUN** locally — they need the WP test library and a live MySQL server, which this sandbox does not have.
- **Task 3 — one Integration test added** (`tests/Integration/HoldsExpireCapacityTest.php`, 1 test): a hold converted by a competing writer before the handler's UPDATE must not release capacity, and a second run must be a no-op. It uses only existing infrastructure (migrations, `App::db()`, raw `$wpdb` inserts in the same style as `BookingFlowTest`); no new fixture class or helper was introduced. **It has never been executed here** (no MySQL); correctness is therefore claimed for the unit level only, and the integration file is unverified until CI runs it.
- **Task 4 — owner decision on `no_show` (final, backend-enforced).** The owner has decided: when staff marks an appointment `no_show`, the slot must **NOT** be released, and this must hold in backend logic, not only in the UI. The code already behaves this way; the earlier D10 conclusion stands and no production code was changed for it. Both backend paths were checked by reading code and tests: **`BookingService::markNoShowByStaff`** is covered by `tests/Integration/Phase7Fr55NoShowRedTest.php:255-256` (manual no-show, asserts `booked_count` and `held_count` unchanged); **`VisitService::markAppointmentNoShow`** (the automatic sweep, reached via `VisitService::processNoShows`) is covered by the same file's `testAutomaticSweepGraceBoundaryNoNotificationAndNoCounterDrift` (:559-598). Both paths are covered, so no test was added.
- **Debts recorded, not fixed:**
  - **JobQueue** (`src/Infrastructure/Queue/JobQueue.php:95-102`) uses the same `CpmsDb::query()` success-as-changed-row pattern when claiming a job (`return $updated ? $row : null;`). Whether a claim race can actually mis-report is **unproven**; this PR does not touch it.
  - **SRS vs state machine:** `SRS.md:472` mentions "no-show + release" without naming the object, which conflicts with `docs/state-machines/appointment.md` lines 30 (T8 side effects: audit only) and 55 (invariant I-1: slot release only on T4/T5/T6). Under the owner's decision the code is correct and the SRS wording is the defect. **The SRS and the state-machine document were deliberately not edited in this PR** — recording the conflict is the scope here; the wording fix is its own change.
  - **B3:** `cpms_slot_holds` still has no unique index on holder + slot, only `u_hold_token` (`src/Migrations/2026_09_05_0001_initial_schema.php:215`); a unique index needs a migration, out of scope.
  - **SQLite-mirror limits:** the unit tests prove statement-level logic only. The mirror supplies `GREATEST()` via a registered SQLite function (SQLite has no such builtin), rewrites `%s`/`%d` placeholders to `?` and binds them, and has no real locking, no InnoDB row locks, no `SMALLINT UNSIGNED` underflow behaviour and no collation semantics. InnoDB lock ordering and inter-worker transaction isolation therefore remain **unproven** by this work.
- **Task 5 — measurement of the red step, and a correction.** Measured over the last 30 completed runs of workflow `378282099` (`Persian five-plugin coexistence (Phase 18)`), job `coexistence-combined-ten`, step 27 "Browser regression — Management Portal province/city cascade + duplicate IDs", **per attempt** (32 attempts across those 30 runs): **success 22, skipped 9, failure 1**. The single failure is attempt 1 of run `42252457572` (my branch, head `af229a3b`). The owner re-ran that failed job and it **passed on attempt 2** of the same run. **Correction:** my earlier claim that this step "failed" in runs `42101211202`, `42105398521` and `42240899891` is **not supported** by this measurement — in those three runs step 27 was **skipped**, not failed. The check-run API is what made the earlier claim look right: it lists a check-run named for the job (which was `failure` in those runs), not the step, so job-level failure was mistaken for step-level failure. ### [2026-11-06] — B1: `FinanceService::refundPayment` lost update (refunded_amount read-modify-write)

- **Class B (pre-existing), not a regression.** `refundPayment` read the payment row without a lock, derived `alreadyRefunded`/`maxRefundable` and validated `refund <= maxRefundable` **before** opening the transaction (`FinanceService.php:695`, `:697-699`, `:703`), then inside `transactional()` locked the row with `findForUpdate` (`:716`) but computed `$newRefunded = $alreadyRefunded + $refund` from the **stale pre-lock** value and wrote it back. Two interleaved refunds both passed the guard from the same pre-transaction read; the second overwrote the first, and `refunded_amount` could exceed the captured amount. `docs/state-machines/payment.md` P3 (`refund_amount ≤ amount - refunded`) was therefore enforced against a stale snapshot.
- **Minimal fix (inside the existing transaction, no schema change, no new index):** after `findForUpdate` the guard is re-derived from the **locked** row — `$paid_amount`, `$already_refunded`, `$max_refundable` — and `$refund > $max_refundable` throws `CLINIC_VALIDATION_FAILED` (422, `max_refundable`) before any write. The same fresh `$already_refunded` feeds `$new_refunded`, the `refunded_amount` write and the `status` transition; the stale `$alreadyRefunded` was removed from the closure's `use` list. The pre-transaction read/validation is kept unchanged as the fast path, so non-concurrent behaviour is identical. Ownership of the audit row and the invoice side (`reverseInvoicePayment` already locks its invoice) are untouched.
- **Test — `tests/Unit/RefundLostUpdateTest.php` (new, pure Unit, no WP/MySQL):** a pattern-matched fake `wpdb` + the real `CpmsDb`/repositories/`FinanceService` under `ScopeContext`. Deterministic interleaving: an `onQuery` hook fires on the payments `… FOR UPDATE` SELECT and runs the second refund to completion while the first holds the lock — both have already done their pre-transaction read, so both writes are in play. Four cases: two interleaved refunds (60 + 70 on a 100 capture), refund above remaining rejected with no state change, retry of the same refund not double-counted, and a positive control (40 then 60 → `refunded`).
- **Before-fix evidence (same test, unfixed code):** `testInterleavedConcurrentRefundsDoNotLoseUpdate` fails — the second refund was accepted and the final `refunded_amount` measured **60**, i.e. the 70 refund was lost and the guard was bypassed; `Tests: 4, Assertions: 16, Failures: 1`. After the fix the same file is `OK (4 tests, 21 assertions)`.
- **Regression check (local, php-wasm PHP 8.5.12 + repo `phpunit.phar` 11.5.56):** full `--testsuite Unit` on this head = **1049 tests, 74 errors, 19 failures, 31 skipped, 1 risky**; pristine `main` (`3fce6a0f`) = **1045 tests, 74 errors, 19 failures, 31 skipped, 1 risky**. The failing-test name sets are **identical (94 names, `diff` clean)** — the delta is exactly my 4 new tests. Those 94 are environmental (php-wasm has no `stream_socket_pair`, no WP/MySQL), **not** attributable to this change.

- **Reader finding 1 — `guardedWrite` must not rely on `last_error` alone. FIXED.** The previous guard compared `last_error` before/after and returned `execute()`'s int, so a write that fails while the driver records **no message** looked like a clean zero-row no-op. The guarded write now bypasses `CpmsDb::execute()` for its own two statements and reads the **raw** `$wpdb->query()` return: `false` is an error on its own, a non-int result is an error, and a non-empty `last_error` is an error — all three throw, which lets `transactional()` roll back that hold (including a status change already made in the same transaction), keeps `$freed` untouched and leaves the hold `active` for a later run. A legitimate zero-row slot release returns the int `0` and is **not** an error, so the hold still expires — pinned by `testLegitimateZeroRowSlotReleaseStillExpiresTheHold`. Prepared SQL still comes from `CpmsDb::prepare()`. **`CpmsDb` itself is unchanged**, so `execute()`/`query()` keep their meaning for every other caller; the only thing this handler skips is the profiler's per-query accounting for its own two statements.
- **Reader finding 2 — silent-failure injection mode. ADDED.** The stub's `writeFault` hook now understands the sentinel `'FALSE_WITHOUT_ERROR'`: `query()` returns `false` and `last_error` is left untouched. Two tests use it (`testSilentFailedHoldUpdateAbortsAndLeavesHoldActive`, `testSilentFailedSlotReleaseRollsBackTheHoldStatusChange`). **Measured RED against the last_error-only guard** (restored by file copy): `Tests: 14, Assertions: 39, Failures: 2` — exactly those two, failing with *a real DB error must abort the run, not be treated as zero affected rows*. **Measured GREEN** with the fixed guard: `Tests: 14, Assertions: 45`. A direct probe of the old guard's data outcome on a silent slot failure shows the damage: `freed=1 hold_status=expired held_count=1` — hold expired and counted as freed while the slot still counted it, so no later run could retry.
- **Reader finding 3 — the Integration test did not exercise the race, and asserted shared fixtures. FIXED by narrowing the claim, not by faking the race.** `tests/Integration/HoldsExpireCapacityTest.php` converted the hold **before** the handler ran, so the handler's own SELECT never returned that row; it would also have passed on the pre-fix handler. Its docblock and test name now say exactly that (`testHoldAlreadyConvertedBeforeRunReleasesNothingAndSecondRunIsNoOp`), and it states that real race coverage lives in the Unit tests (`afterNextSelect` hook). The hard-coded `clinic_id = 1` and the assumption that a primary Location exists for clinic 1 are gone: the test now creates its **own** Clinic, Location (`is_primary = 0`, so it cannot collide with the shared fixture), Clinician, Slot and Hold, and deletes all five in `tearDown` (5 `DELETE` statements).   - **(a) Refunds have no idempotency key.** A retried refund that still fits the ceiling **is applied twice** — nothing matches a repeat request to the original. Captures have `Idempotency-Key` (P1); refunds do not. Owner decision pending; safe default = no change.
  - **(b) A partially refunded payment stays `captured`, so it is still voidable, and `void` reverses the full amount.** `FinanceService.php:750` writes `status = $new_refunded >= $paid_amount ? 'refunded' : 'captured'`; `voidPayment` only requires `captured` (`:612`) and reverses `amount` in full (`:638` `$amount = $this->toMinor(... $payment['amount'])` → `:645` `reverseInvoicePayment($invoice, $amount)`). A payment captured 100 and refunded 40 can then be voided, restoring 100 to the invoice instead of the remaining 60.
  - **(c) Non-integral stored DECIMAL amounts are read as 0 and become unrefundable.** `toMinor()` (`:1210-1225`) returns `null` for any non-whole value (`$f == floor($f)`), and `refundPayment` coerces with `?? 0` (`:697-698`), so a payment stored as e.g. `100.50` yields `paid_amount = 0` and every refund is rejected.
  - **(d) Rows already corrupted by the old bug now get 422 with a negative `max_refundable`.** Where `refunded_amount > amount` from the pre-fix overwrite, `paid_amount - already_refunded` is negative, so the guard at `:739-745` fails for **every** refund and reports a negative `data.max_refundable`. The rows need data repair; no repair is in this PR.
  - **(e) `amount` omitted uses the stale remainder and fails closed under a concurrent refund.** `:700-702` derives the refund from the **pre-transaction** `maxRefundable`; if a concurrent refund lands first, the locked re-check at `:739` rejects with 422 instead of refunding the new remainder. Fails closed — no over-refund — but a legitimate call can be refused.
  - **(f) `docs/state-machines/payment.md` disagrees with the code.** Line 44 describes `refunded` as "تمام/ناقص — Terminal" (terminal for full **or partial**), while `:750` keeps a partial refund at `captured`; and line 51's P3 `refund_amount ≤ amount - refunded` names `amount - refunded` as the ceiling without stating the units or the stale-read caveat. Documentation drift only; no code changed.
  - **(g) `data.max_refundable` is undocumented.** The 422 emitted at `:744` carries `data.max_refundable`, but `docs/api/error-codes.md:32` (`CLINIC_VALIDATION_FAILED`) documents only `data.errors` and never mentions this key or its unit (a whole-currency minor unit as produced by `toMinor`, not a formatted amount). API documentation gap.
- **Fake-wpdb limitation, stated plainly:** the Unit test's fake `wpdb` has **no MVCC and no real row locks** — `FOR UPDATE` is only matched as text, so the test would **also pass with a non-locking re-read**. It proves the code re-derives the guard from the value it reads inside the transaction; it does **not** prove real InnoDB locking, gap-lock or isolation behaviour. **Real InnoDB lock behaviour is unproven** in this PR; only the CI Integration suite exercises MySQL, and it does not run a two-connection refund race.

### [2026-11-07] — PR #328 round 11: Unit Tests red at `989397b2` — two unit files declared the same global `wpdb` class

- **What was red, and where it came from.** The `CI` run for `989397b2` (`42296122301`, attempt 3) failed in `Run unit tests (no WP)` ×3, with the annotation `[failure] Process completed with exit code 1.` and nothing further. The job log was **not retrievable** (blob `EOF`) and — corrected below — **no failure mirror was posted**, so the CI text was never available. The failure was therefore reproduced locally, on wasm PHP 8.5.12 with the repo's own `phpunit.phar` 11.5.56 and `phpunit.xml`.
- **Correction to the round-10 statement.** Round 10 recorded that "no mirror comment existed". That was wrong in its reasoning while accidentally right in its conclusion, and the record needs to be exact: the mirror target is the **pull request's issue comments** (`GET /repos/bia2on2on/doctor/issues/328/comments`), **not** commit comments (round 10 had checked `commits/989397b2/comments`). Listing the PR issue comments returns **30** comments, all created 16:30–16:43Z, with families `ci-authz-coverage, ci-composer-lock-audit, ci-custom-role-{archive,migration,race,races}, ci-heartbeat-recovery, ci-integration-evidence, ci-red1-probe, ci-release-runtime ×2, ci-wpcs-evidence, closure-restore-apply, closure-runtime-php, external-site-acceptance ×2, fp-browser-acceptance, fp-mobile-visual ×7, fp-portal-delegated, fp-portal-journey, pilot-inner-zip, pilot-otp-journey, pilot-responsive-evidence, wp-compat-probe`. The failing run was 21:34–21:44Z, i.e. **after** every comment, and the family `ci-unit-tests` is **absent**. The mirror step does exist in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`Post unit test failures to PR`, `if: failure()`, `--family ci-unit-tests`, reading `/tmp/cpms-unit.log`), so the correct statement is: the mechanism exists, the PR comments were checked in the right place, and **no mirror was posted for this run**.
- **Verified cause (evidence).** Two unit files each declare a class named `wpdb`, and `wpdb` is a global name: `tests/Unit/RefundLostUpdateTest.php:34` declares it **at file load** with **no constructor**, and `tests/Unit/HoldsExpireHandlerCapacityTest.php` declared it lazily inside `setUp` behind `class_exists('wpdb', false)`. Whichever loaded first won. When the refund file won, its fake took over and silently dropped the `PDO` handle this test passes to `new \wpdb($this->pdo)`, so the SQLite mirror never saw the handler's writes and the handler read zero rows. Declaring both is fatal (`Fatal error: Cannot redeclare class wpdb`, reproduced), so the lazy guard turned a hard error into quiet cross-file coupling.
- **Local reproduction before the fix.** File alone `OK (14 tests, 45 assertions)`; refund file alone `OK (6 tests, 41 assertions)`; **both together `20 tests, 61 assertions, 11 failures`**, all 11 in this file: `testPositiveControlExpiredHoldReleasesExactlyOneUnit`, `testSecondRunOnSameHoldDoesNotDecrementAgain`, `testHoldConvertedMidRunDoesNotReleaseCapacity`, `testTwoExpiredHoldsReleaseTwoUnits`, `testCounterNeverGoesNegative`, `testHoldStatusUpdateErrorAbortsWithoutReleasingCapacity`, `testSlotReleaseUpdateErrorRollsBackTheHoldStatusChange`, `testRecoveryAfterDbErrorSucceedsOnTheNextRun`, `testSilentFailedHoldUpdateAbortsAndLeavesHoldActive`, `testSilentFailedSlotReleaseRollsBackTheHoldStatusChange`, `testLegitimateZeroRowSlotReleaseStillExpiresTheHold`. Reversing the file order and adding a third file both still produced 11 failures. A duplicate scan over `tests/Unit/**/*.php` for namespace-less declarations found **only** `wpdb`; no duplicate global functions and no same-namespace class collisions. `dd252eb0` did not contain `RefundLostUpdateTest.php` at all — the file arrived with `main` in the `f744a40a` merge, which is why the collision appeared only at `989397b2`.
- **The fix — one file, `tests/Unit/HoldsExpireHandlerCapacityTest.php`, test-only.** The fake is no longer declared as the global `wpdb`. It is built at runtime as a **uniquely named subclass** (`CpmsHoldsExpireFakeSqlite`) of **whatever `\wpdb` is loaded at that moment**, which is exactly what `CpmsDb::__construct(private readonly wpdb $wpdb)` (`src/Infrastructure/Db/CpmsDb.php:33`) needs either way; if no `wpdb` exists at all, a minimal untyped base is declared first. The subclass reuses the previous stub's method bodies verbatim (so behaviour is unchanged) and overrides every member the handler and `CpmsDb` touch: `prepare, query, get_row, get_results, get_var, insert, update, delete` and `prefix / last_error / insert_id`. **Properties are not redeclared**: property types are invariant in PHP, the two possible parents disagree (the refund fake is fully typed, the minimal fallback is untyped), and redeclaring produced `Type of ...::$prefix must be omitted to match the parent definition` — so inherited properties are dropped from the generated class and inherited as-is. `setUp` now saves `$GLOBALS['wpdb']` **and** the `App::$db` singleton, publishes the fake for the duration of the test, and `tearDown` restores both exactly, including the "was not set" case. Two `ReflectionProperty::setAccessible(true)` calls were removed — no-ops since PHP 8.1 and deprecated in 8.5, which CI's 8.5 lane runs.
- **Nothing was weakened.** No test removed, no test skipped, no assertion changed: the file is still **14 tests / 45 assertions**, own-rows creation and cleanup untouched. `tests/Unit/RefundLostUpdateTest.php` was **not edited** (`git diff --quiet` on it → unmodified), so the other file's own latent faults are untouched and merely no longer able to leak here.

  - file alone — `OK (14 tests, 45 assertions)`
  - hold + refund — `OK (20 tests, 86 assertions)`
  - refund + hold (reverse order) — `OK (20 tests, 86 assertions)`
  - `AppointmentMachineTest`, `RefundLostUpdateTest`, hold (third file, refund loaded before hold) — `OK (47 tests, 134 assertions)`
  - `php -l` — no syntax errors. The one remaining deprecation is pre-existing and unrelated: `PDO::sqliteCreateFunction()` is deprecated in 8.5 and was already present at `dd252eb0`; `phpunit.xml` does not set `failOnDeprecation`.
- **Not CI-equivalent — stated plainly.** Composer cannot be installed in this sandbox (no `php` binary, unreachable package hosts) and the full `--testsuite Unit` run here is **not** CI-equivalent: no MySQL, no sockets, hence environmental errors and skips that CI does not have. These local runs prove the **class-collision** defect and its fix; they do not prove the CI Unit job. **CI is the final proof.**

### [2026-11-07] — capacity double-release fix: hold transitions guarded by affected-rows + slot release coupled in one transaction (PR head)

- **Scope.** Fix for the pre-existing HIGH debt recorded at round 11 (`docs/agent-log.md` above, "Standing debts unchanged": `BookingService.php:1154-1159` / `:852-857` resume/confirm double release, `SlotRepository.php:220-228` unguarded `GREATEST`). No migration; no lock-order change (hold-row write first, slot counter second; no Organization→Clinic prefix added; no opposite order); `JobQueue.php`, 403-vs-404, finance code, and D10 (`no_show` does NOT free capacity) untouched. No new error codes (unexpected real DB errors → existing `CLINIC_INTERNAL_ERROR` 500 via `toBookingException`, documented in `docs/api/error-codes.md`). `rescheduleAs` / `cancel` release paths were NOT rewritten (same guard pattern already applies through `SlotRepository::releaseBooking`, now affected-rows-aware); their transactional context was verified (`rescheduleAs` ~1723 and `cancel` ~2198 run inside a transaction → exception rolls back).
- **Transition table (evidence = code read at this head; "inference" where marked).**
  - create hold → increments `held_count` via `SlotRepository::atomicHold` (`> 0` check) — atomic, unaffected.
  - confirm pre-transaction expiry branch → `UPDATE … status='expired' WHERE id AND status='active' AND expires_at<=%s` — WAS unguarded `CpmsDb::query()` + unconditional `releaseHold` (double release). NOW guarded `guardedCapacityWrite` inside `CpmsDb::transactional` + `releaseHold` only if `affected ≥ 1`; on real DB error → ROLLBACK → `toBookingException` → `CLINIC_INTERNAL_ERROR`; `CLINIC_HOLD_EXPIRED` 422 contract unchanged.
  - resume expiry branch — same shape, same fix (no `expires_at` predicate, matching its prior semantics).
  - confirm in-transaction conversion (`status='active' → 'converted'`) — WAS unchecked `query()` (bool ignored); appointment could COMMIT with the hold still `active` under a hidden soft-mode error. NOW guarded; `affected < 1` → `RuntimeException` → transaction ROLLBACKs → compensation path → `CLINIC_INTERNAL_ERROR` 500.
  - confirm post-rollback compensation (`status='active' → 'released'`) — WAS unchecked; capacity released only if `> 0` but real DB errors were indistinguishable from zero rows. NOW guarded; real error → logged (`booking.hold_release_compensation_failed`), hold NOT released, no blind capacity release; `releaseHold` only on `affected ≥ 1`, itself try/catch'd (`booking.hold_capacity_release_failed`).
  - `HoldsExpireHandler` (worker, fixed in #328) — reference pattern mirrored (`guardedWrite`); unchanged.
  - reschedule / cancel (`releaseBooking`) — unchanged call sites; now protected at the repository layer (below).
  - conversion via `atomicClaim` (`held_count GREATEST(held_count-1,0)`, `booked_count+1`) — unchanged (existing `> 0` success criterion).
- **SlotRepository contract change.** `releaseHold()` / `releaseBooking()` now return `int affected rows` (were `void`) and throw `RuntimeException` on a real driver failure (`false` result, non-int result, or non-empty `$wpdb->last_error`). The `GREATEST(counter-1, 0)` floor and `counter > 0` predicate are kept — they are a floor, not a selector, and were never a fix by themselves; the hold-row transition guard remains the anti-double-release selector. Zero rows is a legal outcome (slot at floor) and returns int `0` without an exception.
- **New guard helpers (mirror-only).** `BookingService::guardedCapacityWrite()` (message prefix `booking hold transition write failed`) and `SlotRepository::guardedCounterWrite()` (`slot hold/booking release failed`) mirror `HoldsExpireHandler::guardedWrite()` (two-signal: `$wpdb->query()` false vs int; `last_error` non-empty ⇒ error). PHPDoc on the former instructs to keep them in sync. Deliberately duplicated, not refactored into a shared base, to keep the diff minimal.
- **Tests, tests-first.**
  - NEW Unit (CI-executable): `tests/Unit/HoldsExpireHandlerCapacityTest.php` — `testReleaseHoldReturnsAffectedRowsAndFloorsAtZero`, `testReleaseHoldOnZeroCounterReturnsZeroWithoutError`, `testReleaseHoldDriverErrorThrowsAndKeepsCounter` (both fault variants: injected message and silent `false`).
  - NEW Integration (CI-only, never run locally — see below): `tests/Integration/HoldCapacityReleaseInterleaveTest.php` — 5 tests (resume sequential/interleaved; confirm sequential [characterization, green on main]; confirm interleaved; confirm conversion driver-failure → rollback + single compensating release). Real two-connection InnoDB interleaving is NOT reproduced (single connection; interleaving via a one-shot `query` filter (priority 11) that runs the production worker inline at the service's transition write, or rewrites the conversion write to a missing table). In-transaction interleaving uses CpmsDb SAVEPOINTs — the nested worker's COMMIT coincides with the outer transaction's. Explicitly does NOT prove InnoDB inter-process isolation, lock semantics, or production latency behaviour.
  - **Valid red (Unit, local, php-wasm PHP 8.4):** with `src/` stashed (main code) and the new tests in place, the 3 new tests FAIL (`null is identical to 1` / `null is identical to 0` / missing exception) — red for the right reason; the other 20 tests in the file stayed green. After `git stash pop`: **23/23 OK (96 assertions)**.
  - **Valid red (Integration, predicted but NOT executed):** no MySQL locally — the four failing assertions are reasoned (pre-fix: unconditional `releaseHold` decrements the wrong holder's capacity; conversion-failure: appointment COMMITs). They must be confirmed red-then-green in CI; until then this evidence is inference, not proof.
- **Local Unit landscape (php-wasm, `auto_prepend_file` PSR-4 shim for missing `vendor/`; `tests/` subprocess-spawn files excluded — CI lane is untouched).** `Tests: 1043, Assertions: 354537, Errors: 16, Failures: 5, Skipped: 31, Risky: 1` — every error/failure is environmental and in files this change does not touch: 5× `ArchivalRaceWorkerFailurePathsTest` (proc_open/spawn unsupported in wasm), 11× `Phase15S3*` (`ext/sodium` secretstream missing in wasm build; AWS SDK not installable — no composer in sandbox), plus 1 socket pair warning + 5 vendor-assertion failures (sodium/S3 availability) — none reference BookingService/SlotRepository capacity. The `BookingException` import is exactly `use ClinicCore\Domain\Booking\BookingException;` (the previous `ClinicCore\Application\Booking\BookingException` import was wrong; corrected). **Transaction boundaries, verified against the WP test bootstrap:** unmarked raw `START TRANSACTION` passes through the query rewriter untouched (real transactions); `/*cpms*/`-marked control statements from CpmsDb are rewritten to SAVEPOINTs nested in the current transaction; coordinator-side tests open a real outer transaction and COMMIT/ROLLBACK at the end; forked workers run production code on a bare disposable connection and raw-COMMIT the implicit transaction opened by the first rewritten savepoint — the same top-level commit semantics production has. Probed on MySQL 5.7.29: SAVEPOINT outside an explicit transaction is accepted; real DDL implicitly commits and destroys prior savepoints (ERROR 1305 on RELEASE after DDL), which is why migrations run first and outside any savepoint. Full local detail recorded for the reviewer in the file docblock.

### Task 1 — the six PatientNameValidationTest failures: cause verification

Evidence re-verified this round (NOT assumed): sticky comment
`ci-integration-failures evidence` (issue comment 6716555566, run
42457709458, attempt 1) and the check-runs/annotations APIs. Verbatim: 5
expectation/assertion failures + 1 error, all in PatientNameValidationTest;
summary line `Tests: 2729, Assertions: 75510, Errors: 1, Failures: 5.
skipped=0`. Note the sticky's head is the ephemeral merge ref `5d1ed006`
(= "Merge ff16ec8 into 9aee8f7a") — the CI integration job merges base+head;
content == ff16ec8 + main.

Code-verified root causes (read paths cited, not assumed):

1. **Address never seeded** (4 of 6). `enroll_current_patient()` accepts
   ONLY first_name/last_name/mobile for local demographics
   (PatientService.php:350-354 intersection), so the fixture never stored an
   address; `assertSame('اصلی', ...)` saw NULL (REST tests; `patientRow`
   returns raw row) / '' ((string)-cast in the service tests). The four
   AFFECTED tests: testExplicitEmptyNameWithOtherFieldAppliesNothing
   (:542), testExplicitNullNameWithOtherFieldAppliesNothing (:562),
   testSelfRestUpdateRejectsEmptyStringFirstName (:893),
   testSelfRestUpdateRejectsNullFirstName (:912).
2. **Two-link scenario enumerated only one candidate** (1 of 6).
   `active_linked_patients_for_user()` (PatientRepository.php:164) enumerates
   via `cpms_patient_user_links` joined to patients+clinics with the
   `clinical_access_identity_predicate()` pil edge — it NEVER reads the
   identity-links table for candidacy. The round-34 fixture added a SECOND
   pil binding (`link_user` for user1 ↔ patient2's identity) but wrote NO
   `cpms_patient_user_links` row for (user1, patient2), so `updateMe()`
   resolved exactly ONE candidate (patient1) and the test hit
   `$this->fail('ambiguous patient selection must not silently pick one')`
   at :659 — CLINIC_SELECTION_REQUIRED was never thrown.
3. **Role-denial fixture threw before dispatch** (1 of 6, the ERROR).
   `linkedSelfWithoutPortalRole()` built the fixture with
   `withPortalRole=false`, so the authorized enrollment itself hit the
   role gate at PatientService.php:286 (enroll requires ROLE_PATIENT) and
   threw `BookingException: دسترسی ندارید` (403) INSIDE fixture construction
   (PatientNameValidationTest.php:156 ← :728 ← :964). The REST
   `requirePatient` 403 denial path the test exists to assert was never
   reached. Fixture order was wrong.

## 2026-11-08 — CORRECTION: `agent-log.md:4860` separate-PR plan superseded — `shape()`/`clean()`/pattern redaction are NOT privacy boundaries (append-only)

- **Superseded recommendation — `docs/agent-log.md` line 4860**, the "Separate-PR plan (not implemented here)" bullet in the preceding entry. Its stage-1 advice to *"publish the already-computed non-value `shape()`/category + errno/SQLSTATE instead of the raw `message`"* is **withdrawn as unsafe and must not be implemented**. Line 4860 and every earlier byte are preserved verbatim; this entry only appends. The preceding entry's description of `shape()` as stripping quotes/digits (line 4857) is likewise too generous and is corrected here.
- **Why it was wrong.** `WpSqlFailureLedger::shape()` (L329–335) applies exactly two substitutions — `preg_replace("/'[^']*'/", "'?'", …)` and `preg_replace('/\d+/', 'N', …)` — then `substr(…, 0, 120)`. It neutralises **only single-quoted spans and ASCII digit runs**. `clean()` (L429–433) applies only `preg_replace('/\s+/', ' ', …)` and `substr(…, 0, $limit)`: it **never redacts anything**. Neither is a privacy boundary, and pattern redaction in general is denylisting: it cannot prove the absence of values it did not anticipate.
- **Re-verified on this checkout under real PHP** (PHP-WASM, synthetic inputs only, no patient data): of 7 value classes — single-quoted, double-quoted, backtick-quoted, unquoted name, unquoted email, Unicode, multiline — **`shape()` leaked a value in 6/7** (only single-quoted was neutralised) and **`clean()` leaked in 7/7**. Double-quoted, backtick-quoted, unquoted and Unicode values therefore survive the very helper the superseded plan proposed to publish.
- **The separate Integration failure-evidence path REMAINS UNFIXED.** `WpSqlFailureLedger` → PHPUnit log → `.github/workflows/ci.yml` "Post failures to PR" (family `ci-integration-failures`) still publishes raw driver `message` text, `insert_field()` literals, full `… for query <SQL>` lines and the InnoDB status dump on any Integration failure. **No ledger, projection or workflow code has been written for it**, and PR #335 does **not** close it — #335 fixed only `BookingService` → `OpLogger` → `day2_booking_busy.py` → Pilot publication. Observed published values remain synthetic CI fixtures; the patient-data exposure is potential, not observed.
- **Mandatory shape of any future fix (replaces the stage-1/stage-2 advice at line 4860).** The published output must be produced by a **fixed, strict allow-list**: a closed set of constant category/event labels, an integer errno, a validated SQLSTATE, and explicitly allow-listed positive-integer identifiers — every other field dropped by default, with **no free-text field carried through at all**. `shape()`, `clean()` and any regex/pattern redaction are **forbidden as the boundary**; they may remain only as internal dedupe/formatting helpers whose output is never published. `role_key`/`clinic_id` literals must be dropped or constrained to that same integer allow-list. **Negative publication tests are required, not optional**: in the already-CI-invoked `bin/test_integration_diagnostics.py` (`ci.yml:756`), assert the *published* bytes contain none of the synthetic short names, numbers, emails, Unicode, single/double/backtick-quoted values, unquoted values, multiline/control whitespace, malformed or unknown fields and legacy rows — and that a direct formatter call cannot bypass the projection. Any change to the mirror step itself still **requires a workflow edit and separate authorization**; it is not permitted in #335.
- **Consistency note.** The PR #335 body was already corrected for this in a prior body-only pass; this append makes the repository record agree with it. The earlier line-4860 text is intentionally left in place as history, not as guidance.
- **Scope and checks.** Documentation-only, append-only: no product code, no workflow, no gate/baseline/ruleset change. Verified zero deletions in `docs/agent-log.md` and that all pre-existing bytes (including line 4860) are unchanged. Pre-push checks and terminal CI for the resulting head are reported in the PR body via REST PATCH/read-back; CI is pending at this append. The two reviews behind this correction are **owner-relayed**, not GitHub approvals. Two independent security reviews of the final head remain required; no merge.
